oh_athens.blurb: Athens is a bouldering area in southeast Ohio, with most of the climbing off Route 33/50 or East State Street around the city. Nearly all of it is bouldering, from V0 to V8, mostly V1 to V4, and the problems include cracks and traverses along with slabs. COAD Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Witches Front, Witches Back and Trailer Park Boulders, and Witches and Trailer Park are the most boulder-dense. The Witches problems are described as fun but sandy, and fall is the best season.

ca_cvpc.blurb: CVPC is a large boulder field in Culp Valley, inside Anza-Borrego Desert State Park in San Diego County, at roughly 3,000 feet. It is all bouldering, spread out in almost any direction you can walk and through the hills around it. Grades run from the easiest through V10, with V0 and V1 making up the bulk and a thin tail of harder problems above V5. Across Culp Valley the boulders are weathered granite with slabs, cracks and overhangs, and the cooler months from late fall to early spring suit it best. Northern Area Bouldering holds the most climbs, followed by Hilltop Boulders.

ca_rocklin_deer_creek_park.blurb: Deer Creek Park sits in an old granite quarry in Rocklin, east of Sacramento and close to Interstate 80. The climbing is bouldering on walls and blocks roughly 10 to 25 feet tall, with many flat landings. Grades run from the easiest through V10, concentrated between V0 and V4, with a handful of hard problems at the top. A fair amount of shade from trees and walls helps on warm days. The Bayou, also called The Graveyard, holds the most climbs, followed by Pacific Street Wall, The Bucket Flake and The Banana.

ca_sonoma_coast_state_park.blurb: Sonoma Coast State Park is a stretch of Pacific coast near Jenner, about 80 miles north of San Francisco on Highway 1. Bouldering makes up over half the climbing, with trad, top-rope and some sport routes on the sea crags. Boulder problems mostly run V0 to V3 and go up to V8, and roped grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, thickest around 5.10. Goat Rock holds the most climbs and includes the Sunset Boulders, a pair of house-sized boulders at the edge of the continent. Dry Creek Sea Crag and Twin Coves come next by climb count.

co_grand_mesa.blurb: Grand Mesa is a basalt-capped mesa in the Grand Junction area of Colorado, at around 10,000 feet. The rock is volcanic basalt, highly fractured overall, so climbable buttresses are uncommon, but where thick flows stand up they make steep, featured walls of good quality. Trad leads, with sport next, and grades run from about 5.7 to 5.12, thickest at 5.10, with a few ice lines as well. Land's End Area holds the most climbs, with seven named walls of buttresses roughly 30 to 80 feet tall, and Flowing Park comes next.
